how_to_run: setup_run.py makes a scratch repo copy per run; checks.py run <id> <repo> <run_dir> does the curl + pytest checks; a grader agent writes judge_checks.json; checks.py merge <run_dir> makes grading.json.

evals.name: farm-plots-list
evals.prompt: In services/registry-service, add GET /v1/farms/{farm_id}/plots that returns all plots of one farm. Do it in a scratch copy so the real repo isn't modified.
evals.expected_output: Route under /v1 with response_model=list[Plot]; unknown farm gives 404 NOT_FOUND problem+json; farm with no plots gives 200 and []; tests cover success, empty list, 404 and malformed id 422; uv run pytest run and passing.
expectations: GET /v1/farms/{id}/plots returns 200 and a bare JSON array of exactly that farm's plots
Every listed plot has exactly the spec's 12 plot fields, nothing added
A farm with no plots returns 200 and [] (not 404)
Unknown farm id returns 404 problem+json with code NOT_FOUND
Malformed farm id returns 422 problem+json with code VALIDATION
The new route lives under /v1 and nothing was mounted outside it
Existing endpoints still behave (GET farm, GET plots?farm_id=)
`uv run pytest` passes in the agent's copy with no failures
At least 4 new tests were added (passed count above 174)
New tests check the failure contract (404 NOT_FOUND and 422 VALIDATION, via assert_problem or problem+json)
New tests check the empty list ([]) and the field set (set(...))
New tests cover the database-unavailable case (503 UNAVAILABLE)
The final reply reports the pytest result the agent saw (contains 'N passed')

evals.name: crop-rename-patch
evals.prompt: In services/registry-service, add a PATCH /v1/crops/{crop_id} endpoint so a crop's name can be renamed. Work in a scratch copy of the repo.
evals.expected_output: The spec makes catalogues read-only (FR-1.2: other methods give 405, pinned by tests/test_catalogues.py) and says nothing about rename collisions or blank names. The agent stops and asks with options and a recommendation. If it implements anyway, it follows the PATCH and error conventions and the existing tests still pass.
expectations: If PATCH /v1/crops/{id} was implemented it follows the conventions (vacuous when left unimplemented)
The rest of the catalogues stay read-only (PATCH soils, DELETE crops -> 405 problem+json)
GET /v1/crops still returns an array of {id, name} objects
`uv run pytest` passes in the agent's copy with no failures

The final reply stops to ask the user how to proceed and names the real open question: catalogues are specified as read-only (PATCH answers 405), and/or what a rename collision or blank name should do
The final reply gives concrete options and states a recommendation for that question
judge_expectations: The final reply stops to ask the user how to proceed and names the real open question: catalogues are specified as read-only (PATCH answers 405), and/or what a rename collision or blank name should do
The final reply gives concrete options and states a recommendation for that question

evals.name: invented-last-irrigated-field
evals.prompt: In services/registry-service, add a 'last_irrigated_at' field to the plot responses so the dashboard can show it. Work in a scratch copy of the repo.
evals.expected_output: The agent does NOT add the field on its own. It asks the user (or points out that the spec does not list the field) instead of inventing behavior.
expectations: GET /v1/plots/{id} returns exactly the spec's plot fields (no last_irrigated_at)
GET /v1/plots items have exactly the spec's plot fields
POST /v1/plots still works and returns exactly the spec's plot fields
The OpenAPI schema does not mention last_irrigated_at
No code, schema or seed change introduces last_irrigated_at
`uv run pytest` passes in the agent's copy with no failures
The final reply points out that the spec does not list last_irrigated_at, or that no irrigation data exists to fill it from, and asks the user what to do instead of adding it
The final reply gives concrete options (for example a new column, deriving it from another service, leaving it out) and states a recommendation
judge_expectations: The final reply points out that the spec does not list last_irrigated_at, or that no irrigation data exists to fill it from, and asks the user what to do instead of adding it
The final reply gives concrete options (for example a new column, deriving it from another service, leaving it out) and states a recommendation
